docs.text: Piper knowledge pack: what Piper can and can't do. (Written into Piper by Claude, so Piper describes itself truthfully.)

Piper's abilities: what Piper can actually do. Read Gmail (personal emails separated from newsletters), mark emails read or unread, read an email out. See today's Google Calendar. Check Instagram followers and posts through Metricool. Tell the weather and time for Morne's location. Answer from Morne's own notes in the knowledge folder, from this knowledge pack, from offline Wikipedia and other libraries, and from the web (DuckDuckGo) when the question needs current information. Study a topic in the background when Morne says "study" or "learn about" something, saving what it reads so it can answer offline later. Do exact maths with its calculator. Work out road distances, travel times and directions using OpenStreetMap when online. Look at the screen when Morne holds Ctrl+Alt with the companion running. Remember facts and preferences Morne tells it.

Piper's limits: what Piper can't do. Piper can't send emails, book appointments, create calendar events or post to Instagram yet. Piper can't remember anything unless it is saved to memory; it doesn't learn from conversations by itself. Piper only studies when asked or when idle-learning from its study list; it never studies "later" otherwise. Piper doesn't know today's news, prices or dates of upcoming events without a web search. Piper's knowledge pack is current to mid-2026 and phone or app menus can change.

Piper's honesty rules. Piper only says it has done something if it actually did it in this conversation (for example, a study job really started, a memory was really saved, a search really ran). It never invents distances, dates, prices or numbers. If it doesn't know, it says so and offers to search or study. It asks for missing numbers instead of guessing.

Piper knowledge pack: Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Contacts, Keep, Tasks). (Written into Piper by Claude, current to mid-2026. Google renames buttons now and then; the settings gear and search bars are the reliable way in.) Gmail: the basics. Inbox tabs: Primary (people), Promotions, Social, Updates. Turn tabs on or off in Settings (gear) > Inbox type / Categories. Archive removes a mail from the inbox but keeps it (find it in All Mail); Delete moves it to Bin for 30 days. Star or mark important to keep track. Snooze hides an email until a chosen time. Undo Send: Settings > See all settings > General > Undo Send, set up to 30 seconds.

Gmail: search like a pro. In the search bar: from:anna@example.com, to:me, subject:invoice, has:attachment, filename:pdf, larger:10M, older_than:1y, newer_than:7d, after:2026/01/01 before:2026/02/01, is:unread, is:starred, in:anywhere (includes Bin and Spam), category:promotions, label:orders. Combine them: from:supplier has:attachment newer_than:30d. Use quotes for exact phrases and a minus sign to exclude: -from:temu.

Gmail: clean up promotions and newsletters. Search category:promotions, tick the box at the top, then "Select all conversations that match this search" and Delete or Archive. Unsubscribe link appears next to the sender name on newsletters. Gmail's Manage subscriptions page (left menu, on newer Gmail) lists senders and unsubscribes in one click. Block a sender: open the email > three dots > Block.

Gmail: filters and labels (automatic sorting). Labels are like folders (an email can have several). Create a filter: click the search options icon in the search bar, enter conditions (e.g. from:orders@shopify.com), Create filter, then choose actions: Skip the Inbox, Apply the label, Mark as read, Forward to, Never send it to Spam. Tick "Also apply filter to matching conversations" to sort old mail too. Manage filters in Settings > Filters and Blocked Addresses.

Gmail: templates, signature and out of office. Signature: Settings > See all settings > General > Signature. Templates: Settings > Advanced > Templates > Enable; then when writing an email, three dots > Templates > Save draft as template. Out of office: Settings > General > Vacation responder, with dates and message. Schedule send: arrow next to Send > Schedule send. Gmail: attachments and Drive. Attachments up to 25 MB; larger files are sent as a Google Drive link automatically. Save an attachment to Drive with the Drive icon on hover. Find big emails to free space: search larger:10M.

Gmail: storage full. Google accounts share 15 GB free across Gmail, Drive and Photos. Check at one.google.com/storage. Free space: search larger:10M and delete, empty Bin and Spam, delete large Drive files (drive.google.com/drive/quota sorts by size), and clean Google Photos. Google One plans add more storage.

Gmail: security. Turn on 2-Step Verification at myaccount.google.com/security. Run Security Checkup there. Check Gmail's "Last account activity" (bottom right of Gmail > Details) to see sign-ins. Google never asks for your password or verification code by email or phone. Suspicious email: check the sender's real address (click the name), don't click links, use Report phishing (three dots). Gmail: keyboard shortcuts (turn on in Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts on). c compose, r reply, a reply all, f forward, e archive, # delete, s star, / search, j and k next and previous, shift+i mark read, shift+u mark unread, g then i go to inbox, ? shows all shortcuts.

Google Calendar: create events. Click a time slot or the Create button. Add a title, time, location and guests (they get an invite). Add Google Meet video conferencing with one click. Repeat: Does not repeat > choose daily, weekly, monthly or Custom. All-day events for birthdays and holidays. Quick add from the search bar style: type "Dentist Friday 3pm" in a new event title and Calendar fills the time. Google Calendar: reminders and notifications. In an event, add notifications (e.g. 30 minutes before, 1 day before) as notification or email. Default reminders: Settings (gear) > Settings for my calendars > your calendar > Event notifications. Tasks appear on the calendar too (Create > Task).

Google Calendar: share a calendar. Settings > Settings for my calendars > choose calendar > Share with specific people > Add people, choose permission: See only free/busy, See all event details, Make changes to events, Make changes and manage sharing. To get a public link, tick Make available to public (careful: anyone can see it). Create separate calendars (e.g. Work, Family) with Other calendars > plus > Create new calendar.

Google Calendar: appointment schedules and time zones. Create > Appointment schedule makes a booking page people can use to book slots with you. Settings > General > Time zone sets your zone; tick Display secondary time zone for travel or customers abroad. The Isle of Man uses UK time: GMT in winter, BST (GMT+1) from late March to late October. Google Calendar: invites and replies. Guests reply Yes, No or Maybe; you see replies under Guests in the event. Propose a new time from an invite. If you edit an event with guests, Calendar asks whether to send updates. Find a time: open the event > Find a time shows everyone's free/busy if they share it.

Google Drive: files and folders. drive.google.com. New > Folder, File upload or Folder upload. Drag files into the browser window to upload. Starred and Recent help you find things. Search with type, owner and date filters. Drive for desktop (Windows app) shows Drive as a G: drive in File Explorer and syncs automatically. Google Drive: sharing. Right-click > Share > add people with Viewer, Commenter or Editor permission; or Copy link and choose Anyone with the link. Restricted means only added people can open it. Stop sharing: Share > change to Restricted or remove the person. Transfer ownership: Share > the person's role > Transfer ownership (within personal accounts it asks them to accept).

Google Drive: recover and versions. Bin keeps deleted files 30 days; restore with right-click > Restore. Version history: File > Version history in Docs, Sheets and Slides, or Manage versions for uploaded files. You can name versions to find them later. Google Docs: writing. docs.new creates a new doc. Headings via Normal text dropdown; the document outline (left) builds from headings. Tools > Voice typing for dictation (Chrome). Comments: select text > comment button; @name assigns it to someone. Suggesting mode (pencil top-right) tracks changes like Word. Download as Word or PDF: File > Download. Ctrl+Shift+C word count.

Google Sheets: the essentials. sheets.new creates a sheet. Formulas start with =. =SUM(A2:A100), =AVERAGE, =COUNT, =COUNTIF(B:B,"Paid"), =SUMIF(B:B,"Paid",C:C), =ROUNDUP(A2/B2,0) for boxes needed, =IFERROR(A2/B2,0), =VLOOKUP or =XLOOKUP to look up a value in another table, =UNIQUE and =FILTER for lists, =TODAY() for the date. Freeze header row: View > Freeze > 1 row. Filter: Data > Create a filter. Conditional formatting colours cells by rules (Format > Conditional formatting).

Google Sheets: order and stock sheets. Typical columns: Order, Product, Quantity, Units per box, Boxes (=ROUNDUP(C2/D2,0)), Full boxes (=INT(C2/D2)), Loose units (=MOD(C2,D2)), Unit price, Total (=C2*H2). Add totals with =SUM at the bottom. Pivot table (Insert > Pivot table) sums sales by product or month. Import from Shopify by exporting CSV and File > Import. Google Slides, Forms and Sites. slides.new for presentations; Present button shows full screen; Speaker notes under each slide. forms.new makes surveys and order forms; responses go into a Sheet (Responses > Link to Sheets). sites.new builds a simple website from Drive content.

Google Meet. meet.google.com or the Meet button in Calendar events. Share the link or dial-in number. During a call: mute (Ctrl+D), camera (Ctrl+E), share screen (Present now), captions, background blur. Free personal accounts limit group calls (3+ people) to 60 minutes; one-to-one calls can run longer. Google Contacts. contacts.google.com. Gmail saves people you email automatically under Other contacts. Create labels (groups) like Customers or Suppliers and email the whole label. Merge & fix finds duplicates. Export as CSV or vCard to move contacts to another phone or service.

Google Keep and Google Tasks. Keep (keep.google.com) holds quick notes, checklists and voice notes, with reminders by time or place and colour labels. Tasks (in Gmail and Calendar side panel) holds to-do items with due dates that show on the calendar. Both sync to the phone apps. Google Workspace for business. Workspace (paid) gives an email at your own domain (you@yourshop.com), more storage, shared drives for teams, admin controls and longer Meet calls. Personal Gmail is free but uses @gmail.com. Setting up needs domain verification in the Admin console.

Google on iPhone. Install Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Docs and Sheets from the App Store, or add the Google account to Apple's Mail and Calendar (Settings > Apps > Mail > Mail Accounts > Add Account > Google). Google Photos backs up iPhone photos if Backup is on in the app (uses the 15 GB storage).

Piper knowledge pack: iPhone and iOS. (Written into Piper by Claude, current to mid-2026, iOS 26. Apple sometimes moves menus between versions; if a step doesn't match, search Settings with the search bar at the top or check support.apple.com.) iPhone basics: on iPhones with Face ID (iPhone X and later, no Home button), swipe up from the bottom edge to go Home; swipe up and pause in the middle to see open apps (the App Switcher); swipe down from the top-right corner for Control Centre; swipe down from the top-left or middle for Notifications. On iPhones with a Home button (iPhone SE), press Home to go Home, double-press for the App Switcher, swipe up from the bottom for Control Centre.

iPhone: take a screenshot. Face ID iPhone: press the side button and volume up at the same time, then let go. Home button iPhone: press the side (or top) button and the Home button together. A thumbnail appears bottom-left; tap it to crop or mark up, or swipe it away to save. Screenshots go to the Photos app, album Screenshots. For a full-page screenshot of a web page in Safari, tap the thumbnail and choose Full Page.

iPhone: record the screen. Add Screen Recording to Control Centre first (open Control Centre, tap the plus at the top-left, Add a Control, Screen Recording). Then open Control Centre, tap the record button, wait for the 3-second countdown. To stop, tap the red indicator at the top of the screen. Long-press the record button to turn the microphone on.

iPhone: turn off, restart or force restart. Turn off: hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, then drag it. Or Settings > General > Shut Down. Force restart when the phone is frozen (iPhone 8 and later): press and quickly release volume up, press and quickly release volume down, then hold the side button until the Apple logo appears (about 10 seconds). Nothing is deleted by a force restart.

iPhone: emergency SOS. Hold the side button and a volume button, then drag Emergency Call, or keep holding to call automatically. Pressing the side button 5 times quickly also starts Emergency SOS. Settings > Emergency SOS controls this. Set up Medical ID and emergency contacts in the Health app (Medical ID).

iPhone: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Settings > Wi-Fi, choose the network, enter the password. To share a Wi-Fi password with a nearby iPhone, unlock yours near theirs while they pick the network; a Share Password prompt appears. Bluetooth: Settings > Bluetooth, put the other device in pairing mode, tap its name. Turning Wi-Fi or Bluetooth off in Control Centre only disconnects until tomorrow; turn it fully off in Settings.

iPhone: mobile data, hotspot and data usage. Settings > Mobile Service (or Mobile Data / Cellular) shows how much data each app uses; you can switch mobile data off per app there. Personal Hotspot: Settings > Personal Hotspot > Allow Others to Join; the Wi-Fi password is shown there. Reset the usage statistics at the bottom of the Mobile Service page at the start of each billing month.

iPhone: battery. Settings > Battery shows which apps use the most battery and Battery Health (maximum capacity; under about 80% means the battery is worn and Apple can replace it). Low Power Mode (Settings > Battery or Control Centre) reduces background activity. Charging limit: newer iPhones let you limit charging to 80% (Settings > Battery > Charging) to make the battery last longer. Show battery percentage: Settings > Battery > Battery Percentage.

iPhone: storage full. Settings > General > iPhone Storage lists what uses space and suggests fixes. Biggest wins: offload unused apps (keeps their data), delete old videos, turn on iCloud Photos with Optimise iPhone Storage (Settings > [your name] > iCloud > Photos), empty Recently Deleted in Photos (it keeps deleted photos 30 days), clear old message attachments (Settings > General > iPhone Storage > Messages), and delete downloaded music, podcasts and Netflix downloads. iPhone: update iOS. Settings > General > Software Update. Plug into power and use Wi-Fi. Automatic Updates can be turned on there. Back up first (see iPhone backup).

iPhone: back up. iCloud backup: Settings > [your name] > iCloud > iCloud Backup > Back Up Now; it backs up automatically each night when the phone is locked, charging and on Wi-Fi. The free iCloud plan is only 5 GB, so most people need iCloud+ (50 GB, 200 GB, 2 TB). Backup to a Windows PC: install Apple Devices from the Microsoft Store (or iTunes on older Windows), connect with a cable, trust the computer, then Back Up Now; tick Encrypt local backup to include passwords and Health data.

iPhone: move to a new iPhone. Quick Start: turn on the new iPhone and put it next to the old one; a Set Up New iPhone card appears; follow it to transfer directly. Keep both on power and Wi-Fi. Alternatively restore from an iCloud backup during setup. Before giving away the old phone: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content and Settings (this also turns off Find My and removes Activation Lock).

iPhone: Apple Account and passwords. Your Apple Account (formerly Apple ID) is at the top of Settings. Change its password: Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Change Password. Saved website and app passwords live in the Passwords app (iOS 18 and later); search for the site, Face ID unlocks it. Turn on two-factor authentication. Apple will never ask for your verification code by phone or text; anyone who does is a scammer.

iPhone: Find My. Turn on in Settings > [your name] > Find My > Find My iPhone, plus Find My network and Send Last Location. To find a lost iPhone, use the Find My app on another Apple device or icloud.com/find on a PC. Mark As Lost locks it and shows a message; Erase This Device wipes it remotely. AirTags and AirPods also appear in Find My.

iPhone: Face ID, passcode and Stolen Device Protection. Settings > Face ID & Passcode. Use a 6-digit passcode or longer. Stolen Device Protection (turn it on there) requires Face ID, not just the passcode, for sensitive changes when away from familiar places, and adds a one-hour delay for changing the Apple Account password. If you forget the passcode, the iPhone must be erased (Forgot Passcode on the lock screen after failed attempts, or recovery mode with a computer); data comes back from backup.

iPhone: notifications and Focus. Settings > Notifications sets each app's alerts; Scheduled Summary bundles less urgent ones. Focus (Settings > Focus, or Control Centre) silences calls and alerts: Do Not Disturb, Sleep, Work, Personal, and custom ones, with allowed people and apps. Silence unknown callers: Settings > Apps > Phone > Silence Unknown Callers (calls go to voicemail), or Call Screening on newer iOS which asks unknown callers who they are.

iPhone: block a caller or texter. In Phone, Recents, tap the info (i) next to the number > Block Caller. In Messages, open the conversation, tap the name at the top > Block. Manage the list in Settings > Apps > Phone > Blocked Contacts. Filter unknown senders in Messages: Settings > Apps > Messages > Screen Unknown Senders. iPhone: Messages and iMessage. Blue bubbles are iMessage (over the internet, Apple to Apple), green are SMS/MMS or RCS (to Android). Long-press a message to react, reply in thread, edit (within 15 minutes) or undo send (within 2 minutes). Schedule a message: tap plus > Send Later. Share your location: tap plus > Location. Turn on iMessage in Settings > Apps > Messages.

iPhone: Camera and Photos. Open the camera quickly from the lock screen by swiping left, or with the Camera Control button on iPhone 16 and later. Tap the screen to focus, slide up or down beside the focus box to change brightness. Hold the shutter for video (QuickTake). Live Text: point at text or open a photo and tap the text icon to copy text, numbers or phone numbers. Hide photos: select > More > Hide; they go to the Hidden album (locked with Face ID). Recently Deleted keeps deleted photos 30 days.

iPhone: AirDrop. Share > AirDrop, choose the nearby person. To receive, Control Centre > long-press the network box > AirDrop > Contacts Only or Everyone for 10 Minutes. NameDrop: hold two iPhones top to top to swap contact details. AirDrop needs Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on. iPhone: Apple Pay and Wallet. Add a card in Wallet > plus. Pay: double-press the side button, look at the phone (Face ID), hold it near the card reader. Boarding passes, tickets and loyalty cards also go in Wallet. If the phone is lost, remove cards via Find My or the Apple Account website.

iPhone: Siri. Say "Siri" or "Hey Siri", or hold the side button. Type to Siri: double-tap the bottom of the screen (newer iOS). Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri controls it. Useful: "Set a timer for 10 minutes", "Remind me to call Anna when I leave", "Read my messages", "Turn on the torch". iPhone: Screen Time and parental controls. Settings > Screen Time shows usage, sets Downtime, App Limits and Communication Limits, and Content & Privacy Restrictions. For a child, set up Family Sharing and manage their Screen Time from your own iPhone. Use a Screen Time passcode the child doesn't know.

iPhone: Accessibility. Settings > Accessibility: Display & Text Size (larger text, bold text), Zoom, Magnifier, VoiceOver (screen reader), AssistiveTouch (on-screen button), Back Tap (double-tap the back of the phone to do an action, e.g. screenshot), Hearing Devices, Live Captions. Text size quickly: Control Centre > Text Size. iPhone: home screen and apps. Long-press an empty area to enter jiggle mode, drag apps, drop one on another to make a folder. Remove an app: long-press > Remove App > Delete App (or Remove from Home Screen to keep it in the App Library). App Library is the last page to the right. Widgets: jiggle mode > Edit > Add Widget. Customise the lock screen by long-pressing it.

iPhone: Safari. Tab overview: tap the tabs button. Private browsing: tabs > Private. Reader view: tap the page menu in the address bar. Clear history and website data: Settings > Apps > Safari > Clear History and Website Data. Block pop-ups and set the search engine in the same Safari settings. iPhone: Mail, Gmail and calendars. Add a Google account to the built-in apps: Settings > Apps > Mail > Mail Accounts > Add Account > Google, then choose Mail, Contacts and Calendars. Or install the Gmail and Google Calendar apps from the App Store. Default mail app: Settings > Apps > Gmail > Default Mail App.

iPhone: Personal safety and scams. Apple, banks and HMRC-style agencies don't ask for codes or passwords by phone. Don't install configuration profiles or 'support' apps because someone told you to. Check Settings > General > VPN & Device Management for unknown profiles. Safety Check (Settings > Privacy & Security > Safety Check) shows and stops sharing with other people.

iPhone: fix common problems. App frozen: swipe it away in the App Switcher and reopen. Phone slow or odd: restart it. No sound on calls: check the Ring/Silent switch or Action button, and Bluetooth (it may be sending audio to headphones). Not charging: clean lint from the port gently with a wooden toothpick, try another cable, check Optimised Battery Charging. Wi-Fi problems: forget the network and rejoin, or Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings (this removes saved Wi-Fi passwords). Recovery mode needs a computer with Apple Devices or iTunes.

Piper knowledge pack: Isle of Man. (Written into Piper by Claude, mid-2026. Only well-established facts. For exact road distances, journey times and directions, Piper uses live OpenStreetMap routing, not these notes.) Isle of Man overview. A self-governing British Crown Dependency in the Irish Sea, between England, Scotland, Wales, Ireland and Northern Ireland. Not part of the UK or the EU. The head of state is the King, as Lord of Mann, represented by the Lieutenant Governor. Population about 84,000. About 33 miles (52 km) long and 13 miles (22 km) wide. Capital: Douglas. Emergency number 999 (112 also works).

Isle of Man government. Tynwald is the island's parliament, often described as the oldest continuous parliament in the world (over 1,000 years). It has the House of Keys (elected) and the Legislative Council. Tynwald Day, 5 July, is held outdoors at Tynwald Hill in St John's, where new laws are announced in English and Manx. The Chief Minister leads the government.

Isle of Man towns. Douglas (capital, largest town, east coast, ferry terminal). Castletown (former capital until 1869, south-east, home of Castle Rushen and the Old House of Keys). Ramsey (north-east, second largest town). Peel (west coast, Peel Castle on St Patrick's Isle, known for sunsets and kippers). Port Erin and Port St Mary (south-west). Onchan (next to Douglas). Laxey (east, the Great Laxey Wheel). Ballasalla (near the airport, Rushen Abbey). Villages include St John's, Kirk Michael, Foxdale, Union Mills and Santon.

Castletown, Isle of Man. A harbour town in the south-east. Castle Rushen is one of the best-preserved medieval castles in the British Isles. The Old House of Keys and the Nautical Museum are here. Castletown is on the Isle of Man Steam Railway line between Douglas and Port Erin. Ronaldsway Airport is just outside, near Ballasalla. Roughly 9 miles from Douglas by road (check live maps for exact distance and travel time).

Isle of Man landmarks. Snaefell (621 m, 2,036 ft) is the highest point; on a clear day you can see England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland from the summit. The Great Laxey Wheel (Lady Isabella) is the largest working waterwheel in the world. Peel Castle, Castle Rushen, Rushen Abbey, the Calf of Man (small island off the south-west tip, a bird observatory), Cregneash (traditional Manx village), the Sound (south tip, seals), Niarbyl, Glen Maye and the many Manx glens. The whole island is a UNESCO Biosphere Region.

Isle of Man transport. Ronaldsway Airport (IOM) near Castletown and Ballasalla, with flights to UK cities. The Isle of Man Steam Packet Company runs ferries from Douglas to Heysham and Liverpool all year, and to Belfast and Dublin seasonally. Bus Vannin runs the buses. Heritage railways: the Isle of Man Steam Railway (Douglas to Port Erin, via Castletown), the Manx Electric Railway (Douglas to Ramsey via Laxey), the Snaefell Mountain Railway (Laxey to the summit), and the Douglas Bay Horse Tram along the promenade.

Isle of Man roads and driving. Driving is on the left. Some roads outside towns have no national speed limit (derestricted), though many roads now have limits; obey the signs. The Mountain Road (A18) between Ramsey and Douglas is part of the TT course and is closed during races. Road closures for racing are published by the Department of Infrastructure.

Isle of Man TT. The Tourist Trophy motorcycle races, held since 1907, run in late May and early June over two weeks (practice week then race week). The Snaefell Mountain Course is about 37.73 miles (60.7 km) of public roads closed for racing. Senior Race Day is a public holiday on the island. Exact dates for a given year are announced by the organisers (iomttraces.com); Piper should check the web for dates rather than guess. The Manx Grand Prix and Classic TT run on the same course in late August.

Isle of Man money and VAT. Currency is the Manx pound, issued by the Isle of Man Government, equal in value to the pound sterling; UK notes and coins are accepted. Manx notes are not usually accepted in the UK, so swap them before travelling. VAT is shared with the UK, standard rate 20%. Income tax rates are lower than the UK, with a tax cap for high earners.

Isle of Man culture. The Manx language (Gaelg) is a Gaelic language being revived; you'll see it on signs. The national symbol is the three legs (triskelion). Manx cats are tailless. Loaghtan sheep are a native breed with four or six horns. Queenies (queen scallops) and kippers are famous foods. Traditional greeting: "Moghrey mie" (good morning). Saying hello to the fairies when crossing the Fairy Bridge is a local custom. Isle of Man time and weather. UK time: GMT in winter, BST (GMT+1) in summer. The climate is mild and windy, rarely very hot or very cold, with the Gulf Stream softening winters. Fog can close the airport and the Mountain Road.

Isle of Man useful services. Manx Care runs health services; Noble's Hospital is in Douglas (Braddan). Police: Isle of Man Constabulary (999, or 101 for non-emergencies). Government services at gov.im. The Isle of Man Post Office issues its own stamps.

Piper knowledge pack: orders, boxes and everyday maths. (Written into Piper by Claude. The numbers in these examples were checked with Piper's calculator. For any new numbers Piper always uses the calculator, never mental arithmetic.) Order maths: how many boxes for an order. You need two numbers: the total units (e.g. 100,080 tins) and how many units fit in one box (the case size, e.g. 24 per box). Boxes needed = total ÷ per box, rounded UP, because a part-full box is still a box. Full boxes = total ÷ per box rounded DOWN. Loose units = the remainder. If the case size isn't given, ask for it; never guess it.

Order maths worked example: 100,080 tins packed 24 per box. 100,080 ÷ 24 = 4,170 exactly, so 4,170 full boxes and none left over. At 12 per box it's 8,340 boxes; at 6 per box 16,680 boxes. Order maths worked example with leftovers: 100,080 tins packed 50 per box. 100,080 ÷ 50 = 2,001.6, so 2,001 full boxes with 30 tins left over, and 2,002 boxes needed in total if the last box goes out part-full.

Order maths: pallets. Pallets needed = boxes ÷ boxes per pallet, rounded up. Example: 2,002 boxes at 40 boxes per pallet = 50 full pallets plus 2 boxes, so 51 pallets. Boxes per pallet = boxes per layer × layers. Check the pallet weight limit too: total weight = boxes × weight per box (plus about 20 to 25 kg for a wooden pallet). Order maths: in a spreadsheet. Boxes needed =ROUNDUP(units/per_box,0). Full boxes =INT(units/per_box). Loose units =MOD(units,per_box). Pallets =ROUNDUP(boxes/boxes_per_pallet,0). In Google Sheets and Excel these work the same.

Order maths: unit cost and order value. Order value = units × unit price. Unit price from a case price = case price ÷ units per case. Example: 4,170 boxes at £12.50 a box = £52,125. Always say whether a price includes VAT. VAT on the Isle of Man. The Isle of Man is in a customs and VAT union with the UK; standard VAT is 20% (some goods are 5% or 0%). Add 20% VAT: multiply by 1.2. Remove VAT from a VAT-inclusive price: divide by 1.2 (NOT multiply by 0.8). Example: £49.99 plus VAT = £59.99; £49.99 including VAT is £41.66 before VAT. The VAT part of an inclusive price = price ÷ 6.

Percentages. X% of Y = Y × X ÷ 100. Increase by X%: multiply by (1 + X/100). Decrease by X%: multiply by (1 − X/100). Percentage change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100. Example: 20% off £100 = £80. A 50% rise followed by a 50% fall does not get back to the start (100 → 150 → 75). Margin and markup. Profit = selling price − cost. Margin % = profit ÷ selling price × 100. Markup % = profit ÷ cost × 100. Selling price for a target margin = cost ÷ (1 − margin). Example: cost £6, target 40% margin: price = 6 ÷ 0.6 = £10. Markup on that is 66.7%. Margins are always lower than markups for the same sale.

Shopify fees and payouts (approximate, check your plan). Payout = order total − payment processing fee (a percentage plus a fixed amount per transaction) − any transaction fee. Profit per order = payout − product cost − packaging − postage. Averages and splitting. Average = total ÷ count. Splitting a bill or stock evenly: total ÷ people, remainder handled separately. Ratios: to split 100 in the ratio 3:2, divide by 5 parts (20 each), so 60 and 40.

Units and conversions. 1 inch = 2.54 cm. 1 foot = 30.48 cm. 1 mile = 1.609 km. 1 kg = 2.205 lb. 1 lb = 453.6 g. 1 stone = 14 lb = 6.35 kg. 1 UK pint = 568 ml. 1 UK gallon = 4.546 litres. 1 US gallon = 3.785 litres. °C to °F: × 9 ÷ 5 + 32. °F to °C: − 32 then × 5 ÷ 9. 1 litre of water weighs 1 kg. Box volume and shipping. Volume = length × width × height. Volumetric (dimensional) weight used by couriers is usually length × width × height in cm ÷ 5,000 (some use ÷ 4,000 or ÷ 6,000); you pay for whichever is greater, real weight or volumetric weight.

Time maths. Hours to minutes × 60. Working days exclude weekends and bank holidays. The Isle of Man has its own bank holidays, including Tynwald Day (5 July) and TT Senior Race Day (a Friday in early June, during TT fortnight), plus most UK ones. Interest and savings. Simple interest = principal × rate × years. Compound: principal × (1 + rate)^years. Monthly payment questions (loans, mortgages) depend on exact terms; Piper should calculate only with the real figures given.

How Piper does maths. Piper never works out numbers in its head. Plain sums are answered by the calculator directly. In longer answers the brain writes [CALC: expression] and the calculator fills in the exact result. If a needed number is missing (like how many tins fit in a box), Piper asks for it instead of assuming.

Piper knowledge pack: Windows PC. (Written into Piper by Claude, current to mid-2026, Windows 11. Windows 10 support ended October 2025; most steps are similar there. If a menu has moved, search for it from Start.)

Windows PC: essential keyboard shortcuts. Windows key opens Start (then just type to search for any app, file or setting). Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo, Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+P print. Windows+V clipboard history (turn it on the first time). Windows+. (full stop) emoji panel. Windows+L lock the PC. Windows+D show the desktop. Windows+E File Explorer. Windows+I Settings. Alt+Tab switch windows. Alt+F4 close the current window.

Windows PC: take a screenshot. Windows+Shift+S opens the Snipping Tool to select an area; the picture is copied to the clipboard (paste with Ctrl+V) and a notification lets you save it. Print Screen (PrtSc) does the same on Windows 11. Windows+PrtSc saves the whole screen to Pictures > Screenshots. Record the screen: open Snipping Tool and choose the video camera. Windows PC: arrange windows. Windows+Left or Right arrow snaps a window to half the screen. Windows+Up maximises, Windows+Down minimises. Hover over a window's maximise button for Snap Layouts. Windows+Tab shows Task View and virtual desktops. Windows+Shift+arrow moves a window to another monitor.

Windows PC: program not responding or frozen. Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager; select the app and choose End task. If the whole screen is stuck, Ctrl+Alt+Delete gives a menu with Task Manager and restart. If the screen goes black or the display freezes, Windows+Ctrl+Shift+B restarts the graphics driver. Hold the power button for 10 seconds only as a last resort; unsaved work is lost.

Windows PC: PC is slow. Restart it (a real restart, not just closing the lid). Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) > Processes shows what uses CPU, memory and disk; sort by each. Startup apps: Task Manager > Startup apps, disable things you don't need at start-up. Free space: Settings > System > Storage > Cleanup recommendations, and turn on Storage Sense. Keep at least 15% of the drive free. Check for updates. Uninstall programs you don't use (Settings > Apps > Installed apps).

Windows PC: updates. Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates. Optional updates (drivers) are under Advanced options > Optional updates. Pause updates for a few weeks there if one is causing problems. Restart when asked; updates often finish during restart, so don't switch off while it says Working on updates. Windows PC: install and uninstall programs. Prefer the Microsoft Store or the maker's official website. Avoid download sites with big Download buttons that are adverts. Uninstall: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > three dots > Uninstall. The winget command (in Terminal) installs apps too, e.g. winget install Mozilla.Firefox.

Windows PC: files and File Explorer. Windows+E opens File Explorer. Home shows recent files; Downloads holds things saved from the internet. Search box top-right searches the current folder. Show file extensions: View > Show > File name extensions. Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin until emptied; right-click a file in the bin > Restore. Zip files: right-click > Compress to ZIP; unzip with right-click > Extract All. Shift+Delete deletes permanently, skipping the bin.

Windows PC: OneDrive. OneDrive syncs Desktop, Documents and Pictures to the cloud if Backup is turned on (OneDrive icon in the taskbar > Settings > Sync and back up). A cloud icon means the file is online only; a green tick means it's on the PC. The free plan is 5 GB. If the PC complains OneDrive is full, either buy storage or turn off folder backup and move files back.

Windows PC: Wi-Fi and internet problems. Click the network icon at the bottom-right. Turn Wi-Fi off and on, forget the network and reconnect. Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset reinstalls network adapters (needs a restart). Restart the router: unplug for 30 seconds. If other devices work but the PC doesn't, it's the PC; if nothing works, it's the router or the internet provider.

Windows PC: printers. Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners > Add device. Most Wi-Fi printers appear automatically when on the same network. Print queue stuck: open the printer > Open print queue > cancel all; if that fails, restart the PC and the printer. Install the maker's app (HP Smart, Epson, Canon) for scanning and ink levels. Windows PC: Bluetooth devices. Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Add device > Bluetooth, put the headphones or mouse in pairing mode, choose it. Sound coming from the wrong place: click the speaker icon in the taskbar and choose the output device (arrow next to the volume slider).

Windows PC: sound and microphone. Speaker icon > choose output. Settings > System > Sound for input (microphone) and output. Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone must allow apps to use the microphone. Troubleshoot: Settings > System > Sound > Troubleshoot common sound problems. Windows PC: display, text size and night light. Settings > System > Display: Scale (make everything bigger, e.g. 125%), resolution, multiple displays (Windows+P switches between duplicate, extend, second screen only). Night light reduces blue light in the evening. Accessibility > Text size makes text alone bigger. Ctrl+mouse wheel zooms in most apps and browsers; Windows+Plus opens Magnifier.

Windows PC: accounts, PIN and passwords. Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options: Windows Hello PIN, face or fingerprint. Microsoft account password reset at account.live.com/password/reset. Local accounts reset with security questions on the sign-in screen. Use a password manager (Microsoft Edge, Google Password Manager, Bitwarden or 1Password) rather than reusing passwords.

Windows PC: security and scams. Windows Security (built in) is enough antivirus for most people; check it at Settings > Privacy & security > Windows Security. Microsoft never phones you about a virus and never shows a pop-up with a phone number to call; that's a scam (close the browser with Alt+F4 or Task Manager). Never let strangers connect with AnyDesk, TeamViewer or Quick Assist. Back up important files. If a scammer had access, disconnect from the internet, run a full scan, and change passwords from another device.

Windows PC: back up. Windows Backup app (Start > type Windows Backup) backs up folders, settings and apps to OneDrive. For a local copy, plug in a USB drive and use File History (Control Panel > File History) or simply copy important folders to it regularly. The 3-2-1 rule: 3 copies, on 2 types of storage, 1 off-site (e.g. cloud). Windows PC: Microsoft Edge and Chrome. Ctrl+T new tab, Ctrl+Shift+T reopen closed tab, Ctrl+W close tab, Ctrl+L address bar, Ctrl+Shift+N (Chrome) or Ctrl+Shift+N (Edge InPrivate) private window, Ctrl+Shift+Delete clear browsing data. Ctrl+D bookmark. Change the default browser: Settings > Apps > Default apps.

Windows PC: Outlook and Word quick help. Outlook: Ctrl+N new email, Ctrl+R reply, Ctrl+Shift+R reply all, Ctrl+F forward, Ctrl+Enter send (may ask to enable). Word: Ctrl+B bold, Ctrl+I italic, Ctrl+U underline, Ctrl+E centre, Ctrl+L left align, Ctrl+Enter page break, F7 spelling. Save as PDF: File > Save As > choose PDF, or Print > Microsoft Print to PDF.

Windows PC: Excel basics. =SUM(A1:A10) adds a range, =AVERAGE, =MIN, =MAX, =COUNT. =ROUNDUP(A1/B1,0) rounds a division up (useful for box counts). =A1*1.2 adds 20%. $A$1 fixes a cell when copying a formula. Ctrl+; enters today's date. Double-click the bottom-right corner of a cell to fill a formula down. Freeze the top row: View > Freeze Panes. Filter: Data > Filter.

Windows PC: connect an iPhone or Android phone. iPhone: install Apple Devices from the Microsoft Store for backups; photos import via the Photos app (Import > From a connected device) after unlocking the phone and tapping Trust. Phone Link (built into Windows) shows texts, calls and photos from Android phones and some iPhone features. Windows PC: shut down, restart, sleep. Start > Power. Restart fixes more problems than Shut down (Windows fast startup means shut down doesn't fully reset). Laptop lid and power button behaviour: Control Panel > Power Options > Choose what closing the lid does.

Windows PC: check specs. Settings > System > About shows the processor, RAM and Windows version. Task Manager > Performance shows the graphics card and memory use. Disk space: File Explorer > This PC. Windows PC: Command line quick help. Open Terminal by right-clicking Start. ipconfig shows network details; ping google.com tests the internet; sfc /scannow (as administrator) repairs Windows system files; chkdsk checks the disk. python --version and py -0 show installed Pythons (Piper needs Python).
